exercises.prompt: Which of the following body-part nouns is grammatically FEMININE without tāʾ marbūṭah?
exercises.explanation: Paired body parts (عَيْنٌ, يَدٌ, رِجْلٌ, أُذُنٌ) are grammatically feminine, whereas single parts (قَلْبٌ, رَأْسٌ) are masculine.

feedback.rule: Paired body parts are unmarked feminines (muʾannath samāʿī).

exercises.prompt: True or False: Nouns ending in feminine alif mamdūdah (e.g., صَحْرَاءُ) or alif maqṣūrah (e.g., كُبْرَى) are diptotes.
exercises.explanation: True. Both feminine endings (ـَاءُ and ـَى) bar tanwīn.

feedback.rule: Feminine alif mamdūdah and alif maqṣūrah are diptote markers.
